name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage destinations in the world, housing the relic of the tooth of the Buddha.
estimated_cost: LKR 2,000 for foreign adults; free for local devotees (subject to official policy)
opening_hours: 5:30 AM – 8:00 PM daily; special puja offerings at 5:30 AM, 9:30 AM, and 6:30 PM

name: Kandy Lake (Kiri Muhuda)
description: An artificial lake built in 1807 by King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe in the heart of Kandy, featuring a scenic perimeter walkway with picturesque hill views.
estimated_cost: Free public access
nearby_attractions: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya
description: Renowned for its collection of over 4,000 species of plants, including a world-famous orchid house, royal palm avenue, and giant Javan fig tree.
location: Peradeniya, approximately 5.5 km west of Kandy
estimated_cost: LKR 3,000 for foreign adults, LKR 100 for local visitors
opening_hours: 7:30 AM – 6:00 PM daily (ticket counters close at 5:00 PM)

name: Udawatta Kele Forest Reserve
description: A historic sanctuary on a hill-ridge above the Royal Palace of Kandy, known for rich birdlife, ancient meditation caves, and towering indigenous trees.
location: Behind Temple of the Tooth, Kandy
estimated_cost: LKR 1,000 for foreign tourists, LKR 50 for local residents
nearby_attractions: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

name: Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue
description: A gigantic 88-foot white seated Buddha statue atop Bahirawa Kanda hill, offering spectacular panoramic vistas over Kandy lake and surrounding mountains.
estimated_cost: LKR 300 temple donation

name: Kandy Lake Club Cultural Dance Show
description: An authentic 1-hour cultural spectacle showcasing traditional Kandyan drumming, masked devil dancing, acrobatic leaping, and barefoot fire-walking.
estimated_cost: LKR 2,500 / $8 per person
opening_hours: Daily shows at 5:00 PM and 5:30 PM

name: Nine Arches Bridge
description: A famous colonial-era stone railway viaduct surrounded by lush green tea hills and cloud forests, constructed entirely of stone and cement without steel.
location: Demodara, approximately 3 km from Ella town
estimated_cost: Free access (walking along trails/tracks)
opening_hours: Open 24 hours; recommended during daylight train crossing hours

name: Little Adam's Peak (Punchi Sri Pada)
description: An easily accessible hill offering panoramic 360-degree views of the Ella Gap, Ravana Falls valley, and surrounding tea estates.
estimated_cost: Free for regular trail hike; zip-line activities charge separately
opening_hours: Open 24 hours; sunrise (5:30 AM) and sunset (5:30 PM) recommended

name: Ravana Falls & Ravana Cave
description: A popular, scenic 25-meter high cascading waterfall located along the main road, linked to the historic Ramayana legend of King Ravana.
estimated_cost: Free viewing from observation points; small fee for cave entrance

name: Halpewatte Tea Factory & Estate
description: The largest tea producer in the Uva region, offering guided factory tours explaining the orthodox black tea manufacturing process from leaf to cup.
estimated_cost: LKR 1,500 / $5 including factory tour and tea tasting

name: Ella Rock High Altitude Trek
description: A rewarding 4-hour trek through railway tracks, rubber plantations, and eucalyptus forests leading to dramatic sheer cliff views overlooking the Ella valley.
estimated_cost: Free hiking trail (optional local trail guide LKR 2,500)
opening_hours: Best started at dawn (6:00 AM – 7:30 AM) to avoid afternoon mist

name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress (Lion Rock)
description: An ancient 5th-century palace complex and rock fortress built by King Kashyapa, rising 180 meters with world-renowned frescoes, mirror wall, and water gardens.
estimated_cost: USD 36 / approx LKR 11,000 for foreign tourists; LKR 100 for locals
opening_hours: 6:30 AM – 5:30 PM daily (ticket counter closes at 5:00 PM)

name: Pidurangala Rock
description: A massive geological rock formation adjacent to Sigiriya, housing a historic cave temple with a reclining Buddha and offering the most iconic panoramic view of Sigiriya Rock Fortress.
estimated_cost: LKR 1,000 entrance fee (temple donation ticket)
opening_hours: 5:00 AM – 6:00 PM daily (popular for sunrise from 5:30 AM)

name: Dambulla Royal Cave Temple & Golden Buddha
description: The largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka, featuring five sanctuaries under an immense overhanging rock filled with 153 Buddha statues and ancient murals.
estimated_cost: LKR 2,000 / $7 for foreign adults
opening_hours: 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM daily (modest dress covering shoulders & knees required)

name: Hiriwadunna Authentic Village Experience
description: Immersive rural Sri Lankan village safari involving a bullock cart ride, catamaran lake cruise through lotus blooms, and an authentic wood-fired clay pot cooking demonstration on banana leaves.
estimated_cost: LKR 4,500 / $15 per person with organic village lunch

name: Minneriya National Park Elephant Gathering Safari
description: Famed for 'The Gathering'—the largest concentration of Asian wild elephants in the world, gathering around the ancient Minneriya tank reservoir during the dry season.
estimated_cost: USD 45 - 60 per person (including 4x4 safari jeep and park entry)
opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM daily (afternoon 2:30 PM – 6:00 PM is best for elephants)

name: Galle Fort (Dutch Fort & Ramparts)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage fortress built initially by the Portuguese in 1588 and extensively fortified by the Dutch in the 17th century, featuring living colonial heritage.
estimated_cost: Free access to fort ramparts and streets; individual museum fees apply
opening_hours: Open 24 hours; shops and museums typically open 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM

name: Galle Fort Lighthouse & Flag Rock
description: An iconic 26.5-meter coastal lighthouse standing at Point Utrecht Bastion within Galle Fort, surrounded by palm trees and ocean views.
estimated_cost: Free viewing from outside; interior generally not open to public

name: National Maritime Museum
description: Located inside a 1671 Dutch warehouse in Galle Fort, showcasing underwater archaeological artifacts, shipwreck relics, and marine ecosystem exhibits.
estimated_cost: LKR 1,500 for foreign adults, LKR 50 for locals
opening_hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Tuesday to Saturday (Closed Sunday & Monday)

name: Jungle Beach & Rumassala Peace Pagoda
description: A secluded coastal bay nestled beneath the forested Rumassala headland, featuring calm crystal-clear waters for swimming and a tranquil Japanese Peace Pagoda overlooking Galle harbour.
estimated_cost: Free public access

name: Horton Plains National Park & World's End
description: A protected highland plateau at 2,100m elevation featuring montane cloud forests, sambar deer, Baker's Falls, and the sheer 880m vertical precipice known as World's End.
estimated_cost: USD 35 / approx LKR 10,500 for foreign adults
opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily (crucial to enter before 8:00 AM before clouds cover the viewpoint)

name: Pedro Tea Estate & Lovers Leap Waterfall
description: Historic tea plantation founded in 1885 nestled beneath Mount Pidurutalagala, combined with a short trail to Lovers Leap cascade.
location: Pedro Estate, Upper Lake Road, Nuwara Eliya
estimated_cost: LKR 1,000 for tea factory tour & tasting; free waterfall trail

name: Lake Gregory Recreational Waterfront
description: A picturesque mountain reservoir established in 1873 by Governor William Gregory, offering swan paddle boats, horse riding, cycling paths, and cool highland gardens.
estimated_cost: LKR 500 entrance fee; water activities priced separately

name: Victoria Park & Colonial Post Office
description: Meticulously manicured public gardens established for Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee, alongside the iconic red-brick Tudor-style 1894 Nuwara Eliya Post Office.
location: Queen Elizabeth Drive, Nuwara Eliya Town
estimated_cost: LKR 500 entrance fee for park; free post office viewing

name: Yala National Park Leopard & Wildlife 4x4 Safari
description: Sri Lanka's most celebrated national park holding the highest leopard density in the world, alongside wild elephant herds, sloth bears, spotted deer, and saltwater crocodiles.
estimated_cost: USD 65 - 90 per person (includes 4x4 safari jeep, certified wildlife tracker, and wildlife conservation entry)
opening_hours: Morning safari: 6:00 AM – 10:00 AM; Afternoon safari: 2:30 PM – 6:00 PM

name: Sithulpawwa Ancient Rock Monastery
description: A 2,200-year-old Buddhist hermitage located deep inside Yala sanctuary where thousands of monks meditated in rocky grottoes surrounded by roaming wildlife.
location: Deep Yala Jungle Reserve, Southern Province
estimated_cost: Free access (donations welcome)

name: Tissa Wewa Lake & Giant Ancient Stupa
description: An immense ancient irrigation reservoir constructed in the 3rd century BC surrounded by century-old rain trees full of fruit bats, egrets, and peaceful sunset water vistas.
estimated_cost: Free public access
opening_hours: Open 24 hours (dusk 5:00 PM – 6:30 PM is magical)

name: Mirissa Blue Whale & Dolphin Watching Ocean Safari
description: An exhilarating early-morning offshore boat expedition along the southern continental shelf to spot the majestic Blue Whale—the largest creature on Earth—along with sperm whales and spinner dolphins.
estimated_cost: USD 45 - 60 / LKR 14,000 per person including boat, life jacket, and light breakfast
opening_hours: Daily boat departures strictly at 6:30 AM (season: November through April)

name: Coconut Tree Hill
description: A picturesque reddish-cliff dome overlooking the turquoise Indian Ocean, densely covered in leaning coconut palms. One of Sri Lanka's most iconic sunrise and sunset photography spots.
estimated_cost: Free public access
opening_hours: Open 24 hours (best at 6:00 AM sunrise or 5:30 PM sunset)

name: Secret Beach Mirissa
description: A secluded tropical cove sheltered by coastal reefs creating natural turquoise tidal lagoons, ideal for safe swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing with fresh coconuts away from the crowds.
estimated_cost: Free beach access; snorkel gear rental available locally

name: Weligama Bay Surfing & Traditional Stilt Fishermen
description: A wide sheltered sandy bay offering gentle rolling waves ideal for beginner surf lessons, alongside the traditional coastal practice of stilt fishing perched above the ocean shallows.
location: Weligama Bay (5 km west of Mirissa)
estimated_cost: Surf lesson with board & instructor LKR 3,500 - 5,000 / $15

name: Ruwanwelisaya Great White Stupa
description: A monumental 2nd-century BC Buddhist hemispherical stupa standing 103 meters tall with an elephant wall of 344 sculpted pachyderms, revered as one of the world's ancient architectural wonders.
location: Sacred City of Anuradhapura, North Central Province
estimated_cost: Covered by Anuradhapura Central Cultural Fund ticket (USD 25) or free temple area pass

name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi Sacred Fig Tree
description: The oldest living human-planted tree in the world with a recorded planting date of 288 BC, brought from Bodh Gaya, India by Sanghamitta Theri as a sapling from the tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment.
estimated_cost: Included in Sacred City pass or small temple offering

name: Mihintale Sacred Mountain Peak & Monastic Ruins
description: The revered cradle of Buddhism in Sri Lanka where King Devanampiya Tissa met Arhat Mahinda in 247 BC, featuring 1,840 granite steps, monastic hospital ruins, and the summit rock offering 360° jungle vistas.
estimated_cost: LKR 1,000 entrance fee for foreign visitors

name: Gal Vihara (Rock Temple of the Colossal Buddhas)
description: A masterwork of ancient Sinhalese granite carving, featuring four colossal Buddha figures sculpted out of a single granite rock face, including a breathtaking 14-meter reclining Buddha.
location: Ancient City of Polonnaruwa, North Central Province
estimated_cost: Included in Polonnaruwa UNESCO ticket (USD 25)

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage & Sacred Quadrangle (Dalada Maluwa)
description: An exquisite circular stone relic house with four flight steps guarded by intricate moonstones and guardstones, preserving the golden age of medieval Sri Lankan royal civilization.
estimated_cost: Included in UNESCO ticket

name: Koneswaram Temple & Swami Rock (Lover's Leap)
description: A magnificent classical Hindu temple perched dramatically atop Swami Rock cliff 130 meters above the turquoise Indian Ocean, celebrated as the 'Temple of a Thousand Pillars'.
estimated_cost: Free entrance (modest dress required); small shoe keeping fee
opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM daily
activities: Feeding sacred spotted deer in the fort

name: Pigeon Island National Marine Park & Snorkeling
description: One of Sri Lanka's premier marine reserves containing pristine shallow coral reefs teeming with friendly blacktip reef sharks, green sea turtles, and over 300 reef fish species.
estimated_cost: USD 35 - 50 per person (includes park entry permit, boat transfer, and snorkel gear)
opening_hours: 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM daily (season: March to October)

name: Nilaveli & Marble Beach Coastal Relaxation
description: Pure white sand beaches and calm, azure crystal waters sheltered in natural coves, famous for tranquil swimming and fresh seafood dining on the beach.
estimated_cost: Free public access

name: Madu Ganga Mangrove River Boat Safari
description: A scenic motorized boat journey through complex mangrove tunnels and 64 tranquil islands, visiting a historic cinnamon-peeling island and a 200-year-old Buddhist island monastery.
estimated_cost: LKR 5,000 / $16 per private boat (up to 4 people)

name: Bentota Lagoon Water Sports Center
description: Sri Lanka's water sports capital where the Bentota River meets the Indian Ocean, offering thrilling jet skiing, banana boat rides, wakeboarding, and kayaking.
estimated_cost: Jet ski (15 mins) approx LKR 6,000 / $20; kayaking LKR 2,000

name: Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project
description: A pioneering marine turtle conservation hatchery that protects sea turtle nesting beaches, rehabilitates injured turtles, and releases baby hatchlings into the ocean at sunset.
location: Galle Road, Kosgoda (10 km south of Bentota)
estimated_cost: LKR 1,500 / $5 per adult supporting conservation work
opening_hours: 8:00 AM – 6:30 PM daily (sunset baby turtle release at 6:00 PM)

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: One of the most sacred Hindu pilgrimage temples in Sri Lanka dedicated to Lord Murugan, celebrated for its golden gopuram entrance towers, ornate brass carvings, and profound devotional puja rituals.
estimated_cost: Free entrance (men remove shirts; modest attire required for all)
opening_hours: 4:30 AM – 5:00 PM daily (special puja at 4:30 AM, 10:00 AM, and 4:30 PM)

name: Jaffna Dutch Fort & Coastal Lagoon Ramparts
description: An imposing pentagonal limestone fortress built by the Portuguese in 1618 and reinforced by the Dutch, overlooking the Jaffna lagoon and Pannai causeway.
estimated_cost: Free public access

name: Casuarina Beach & Karainagar Island
description: Famed for its powdery white sands, shallow calm turquoise waters, and shady casuarina tree groves along the northern tip of the Jaffna peninsula.
location: Karainagar Island (accessed via coastal causeway from Jaffna)
estimated_cost: LKR 100 parking / entrance fee

name: Gangaramaya Temple & Seema Malaka (Beira Lake)
description: One of Colombo's most prominent Buddhist temples, known for an eclectic blend of Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian, and Chinese architecture, plus a museum of antique artifacts.
estimated_cost: LKR 500 for foreign visitors; free for local devotees

name: National Museum of Colombo
description: Sri Lanka's premier cultural institution established in 1877, exhibiting the royal throne and crown of the Kandyan monarchs along with prehistoric and medieval artifacts.
location: Sir Marcus Fernando Mawatha, Cinnamon Gardens, Colombo 07
estimated_cost: LKR 1,500 for foreign adults, LKR 50 for locals

name: Galle Face Green Oceanside Promenade
description: A 5-hectare oceanside urban park stretching along the coast in the heart of Colombo, popular for ocean breezes, kite flying, and street food like isso vade.
estimated_cost: Free public access
opening_hours: Open 24 hours; liveliest from 4:30 PM to 10:00 PM

name: Pettah Floating Market & Jami Ul-Alfar Red Mosque
description: A vibrant sensory exploration through Pettah's bustling trade streets, stopping at the stunning candy-striped red and white 1908 Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque and waterside wooden pavilions.
location: Main Street & Bastian Mawatha, Pettah, Colombo 11
estimated_cost: Free walking access; food and goods at local market prices

name: Negombo Lagoon & Dutch Hamilton Canal Boat Tour
description: A serene motorboat excursion through the mangrove estuaries of Negombo lagoon and the 18th-century Dutch-built Hamilton Canal, watching fishermen harvest lagoon crabs and prawns.
estimated_cost: LKR 4,500 / $15 per private boat

name: Negombo Lellama Traditional Fish Market & Catamarans
description: A bustling early-morning sensory spectacle where hundreds of ocean catamarans (oruwa) with billowing sails return to shore with their daily catch, spread across the golden sands.
estimated_cost: Free public access
opening_hours: 5:30 AM – 9:30 AM daily (arrive early at 6:30 AM)

name: Arugam Bay Main Point Surfing & Lagoon
description: World-famous right-hand point break attracting surfers globally from May through September, alongside relaxed beach cafes and lagoon sunsets.
location: Main Beach Road, Arugam Bay, Eastern Province
estimated_cost: Surfboard rental approx LKR 1,500 - 2,500 / day
opening_hours: Dawn to dusk (best waves early morning)

name: Crocodile Rock & Elephant Lagoon Safari
description: A short coastal hike leading across sand dunes and an elephant-inhabited freshwater lagoon to a massive granite boulder offering sweeping coastline vistas.
estimated_cost: Free public hiking access (local guide recommended LKR 2,000)
opening_hours: Best at late afternoon 4:00 PM – 6:30 PM
